speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a scalp and forehead rash; to help identify the cause, how long have you had these symptoms and have they spread?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap).

Although your baby's father has psoriasis, the presentation of a red, scaly rash that worsens in cold weather and appears in the first few weeks of life is most consistent with infantile seborrheic dermatitis. Since the rash is located on the scalp and forehead, I would like to see an image of the affected area to confirm the findings before starting treatment. REQUEST IMAGES
